package_info.why_malicious: These versions contain a critical vulnerability (CVE-2024-5655) that allows any user to execute pipelines as any other user, enabling arbitrary code execution within the CI/CD environment without proper authorization. This can be exploited to run malicious code, exfiltrate data, or disrupt services.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During pipeline execution, the code reads the /etc/passwd file and sends its contents via HTTP POST to an external attacker-controlled server, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code exfiltrates sensitive system files to an external server, which is a classic indicator of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal CI/CD jobs should not access or transmit sensitive system files to external locations. The pipeline should only perform build/test/deploy tasks relevant to the project.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate jobs may upload build artifacts to trusted servers, but never system files to untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST to non-corporate domain
No legitimate business reason for this data flow

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During pipeline execution, the code accesses the CI_JOB_TOKEN environment variable and sends its value to an external server via HTTP POST, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating CI/CD tokens can allow attackers to impersonate jobs, access internal APIs, or escalate privileges.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: CI_JOB_TOKEN should only be used internally for authorized API calls, not sent to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Tokens may be used for internal API authentication, but never sent to untrusted endpoints.
key_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST to attacker domain
No legitimate use for externalizing internal tokens

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages CVE-2024-5655 to trigger a pipeline as any user, injecting malicious code into the pipeline definition.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code in the CI/CD environment

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes during the pipeline, exfiltrating sensitive files and tokens to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive data and credentials, enabling further compromise or lateral movement

behavioral_signatures: Pipeline jobs accessing sensitive system files (e.g., /etc/passwd, ~/.ssh/)
Pipeline jobs reading and transmitting environment variables like CI_JOB_TOKEN
Outbound network requests to non-corporate or untrusted domains during CI/CD execution
file_indicators: .gitlab-ci.yml jobs containing curl/wget to external domains
Pipeline scripts referencing sensitive files or environment variables
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from CI/CD runners to unknown or attacker-controlled domains
Unusual traffic patterns from CI/CD infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor pipeline job definitions and execution logs for commands that access sensitive files or environment variables and transmit them externally. Flag any outbound network requests to untrusted domains from CI/CD runners. Audit .gitlab-ci.yml files for suspicious script sections, especially those using curl, wget, or similar tools to send data outside the organization.
